> **Ritu cohort — Local/Early stage only.** This page repeats the Jiaxuan whole-cohort analysis on the subset of patients with `tumor_stage == "Local/Early"` (stage I–II / local / neoadjuvant). All 621 advanced/metastatic patients are excluded, leaving **N = 322** (189 carboplatin, 133 cisplatin). `tumor_stage` is dropped from Table 1 and from every adjuster set because it is constant within this cohort. The exposure and the adjuster set are otherwise unchanged from the Jiaxuan project.
>
> **Only the long-horizon kidney outcomes are modelled on this page.** AKI within 1 year and the CKD composite are carried through Fine-Gray competing-risk models in Section 4, with death at any time as the competing event. The 90-day adverse-event, hospitalization and 90-day-death models this page used to carry have been removed; those outcomes are still derived in [Data Management](ritu_data.qmd) and remain in the saved master, they are simply no longer modelled. **Read both models with their event counts in view** — 51 AKI and 26 CKD-composite events in 322 patients against ~20 covariate degrees of freedom, so both are over-parameterised. See `RITU_PROJECT.md`.

# 1 Setup {.content-hidden}

```{r}
#| label: setup-ritu-whole
# Force UTF-8 locale so kable captions and other strings render real Unicode
# (e.g. em-dash) instead of <U+2014> escape sequences.
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_ALL", "en_US.UTF-8"))
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidycmprsk)
library(ggsurvfit)
library(gtsummary)
library(tableone)
library(flextable)
library(rvg)
library(officer)
library(patchwork)

# Output directory for downloadable Word tables (placed under docs/ so the
# rendered website can serve them from ../tables/whole/<name>.docx).
docx_dir <- "docs/tables/whole"
dir.create(docx_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Output directory for editable PowerPoint copies of every figure. A knitr
# plot hook (defined below) saves last_plot() to docs/pptx/whole/<label>.pptx
# and appends a download link after the figure in the rendered HTML.
dir.create("docs/pptx/whole", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
pptx_dir <- normalizePath("docs/pptx/whole", mustWork = TRUE)
# Relative path for download links from rendered docs/qmd/*.html
pptx_rel_prefix <- "../pptx/whole/"

# Persist the chunk-label -> pptx-path mapping so the chunk hook can emit
# the download link only when the .pptx was actually written.
.pptx_written <- new.env()
.pptx_pair    <- new.env()

# Save one ggplot to <path> as an editable PPTX (rvg::dml).
.save_pptx <- function(p, path) {
  tryCatch({
    doc <- officer::read_pptx()
    doc <- officer::add_slide(doc, layout = "Title and Content",
                              master = "Office Theme")
    doc <- officer::ph_with(doc, rvg::dml(ggobj = p),
                            location = officer::ph_location_type(type = "body"))
    print(doc, target = path)
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) FALSE)
}

# fig.process runs in the chunk eval context. For stacked helpers, the helper
# stashes .pptx_pair[[label]] = list(default=p, fine=p_fine) so we can write
# two PPTX files. Otherwise fall back to last_plot() and one file.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.process = function(filename) {
  label <- knitr::opts_current$get("label")
  if (is.null(label)) return(filename)
  pair <- .pptx_pair[[label]]
  if (!is.null(pair) && inherits(pair$default, "ggplot") && inherits(pair$fine, "ggplot")) {
    p1 <- file.path(pptx_dir, paste0(label, ".pptx"))
    p2 <- file.path(pptx_dir, paste0(label, "_10pct.pptx"))
    ok1 <- .save_pptx(pair$default, p1)
    ok2 <- .save_pptx(pair$fine,    p2)
    rels <- c(if (ok1) paste0(pptx_rel_prefix, label, ".pptx"),
              if (ok2) paste0(pptx_rel_prefix, label, "_10pct.pptx"))
    if (length(rels)) .pptx_written[[label]] <- rels
    return(filename)
  }
  p <- tryCatch(ggplot2::last_plot(), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(p) || !inherits(p, "ggplot")) return(filename)
  pptx_path <- file.path(pptx_dir, paste0(label, ".pptx"))
  if (.save_pptx(p, pptx_path)) {
    .pptx_written[[label]] <- paste0(pptx_rel_prefix, label, ".pptx")
  }
  filename
})

# A "chunk" hook fires after the whole chunk is rendered: append download link(s).
local({
  default_chunk_hook <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("chunk")
  knitr::knit_hooks$set(chunk = function(x, options) {
    out <- default_chunk_hook(x, options)
    label <- options$label
    if (!is.null(label) && !is.null(.pptx_written[[label]])) {
      rel <- .pptx_written[[label]]
      if (length(rel) == 2) {
        link <- sprintf(
          '\n\n<p style="margin-top:-0.5em;font-size:0.9em;"><a href="%s" download>📊 Download top plot as PowerPoint</a> · <a href="%s" download>📊 Download bottom (10 %% ticks)</a></p>\n\n',
          rel[1], rel[2])
      } else {
        link <- sprintf(
          '\n\n<p style="margin-top:-0.5em;font-size:0.9em;"><a href="%s" download>📊 Download as PowerPoint (editable)</a></p>\n\n',
          rel[1])
      }
      out <- paste0(out, link)
    }
    out
  })
})

# Save a gtsummary table to a Word document.
# --- Sparse-outcome guard (Ritu cohort) --------------------------------------
# Restricting to Local/Early disease leaves several outcomes with very few
# events (90-day death = 2; thrombocytopenia grade 3 and the individual
# hospitalization reasons are in the single digits). A model that cannot be
# estimated raises an error, which would abort the entire render, so every
# table / row / figure helper is wrapped below. On success the output is exactly
# what the Jiaxuan version produces; on failure a short note is emitted in place
# of the table or figure. No model specification is changed.
.wrap_tbl <- function(f) {
  force(f)
  function(...) tryCatch(f(...), error = function(e) knitr::asis_output(paste0(
    "\n::: {.callout-warning}\n",
    "## Model not estimable in this cohort\n\n",
    "Too few events among the ", nrow(dat), " Local/Early patients to fit ",
    "this model with the full adjuster set.\n\n",
    "Error: `", conditionMessage(e), "`\n:::\n")))
}
.wrap_row <- function(f) {
  force(f)
  function(time_var, status_var, label, ...) tryCatch(
    f(time_var, status_var, label, ...),
    error = function(e) {
      ev <- tryCatch(
        sum(as.character(dat[[status_var]]) == "1", na.rm = TRUE),
        error = function(e2) NA_integer_)
      tibble::tibble(
        Outcome = label, Model = "not estimable",
        N = NA_integer_, `Excluded (missing cov.)` = NA_integer_,
        Events = as.integer(ev),
        `(sub)HR (95% CI)` = "not estimable", `p-value` = "\u2014")
    })
}
.wrap_plot <- function(f) {
  force(f)
  function(...) tryCatch(f(...), error = function(e)
    ggplot2::ggplot() +
      ggplot2::annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, size = 3.4, lineheight = 1.3,
        label = paste0("Model not estimable in this cohort\n",
                       "(too few events among the ", nrow(dat),
                       " Local/Early patients)\n\n",
                       strwrap(conditionMessage(e), width = 60,
                               prefix = "\n", initial = ""))) +
      ggplot2::theme_void())
}

# Table 1 via tableone. Factor-like columns (factor / character / logical and
# indicator columns of 0/1) are summarised as n (%); every other numeric column
# as median [IQR], except the variables named in `normal_vars` (mean (SD)).
# Categorical variables with any observed cell < 5 get Fisher's exact test.
tableone_mat <- function(d, strata = NULL, normal_vars = "age") {
  d     <- as.data.frame(d)
  vars  <- setdiff(names(d), strata)
  is_fl <- vapply(d[vars], function(x)
    is.factor(x) || is.character(x) || is.logical(x) ||
      (is.numeric(x) && all(stats::na.omit(unique(x)) %in% c(0, 1))),
    logical(1))
  fct_vars  <- vars[is_fl]
  cont_vars <- vars[!is_fl]

  if (is.null(strata)) {
    tab   <- tableone::CreateTableOne(vars = vars, data = d,
                                      factorVars = fct_vars, test = FALSE)
    small <- NULL
  } else {
    tab <- tableone::CreateTableOne(
      vars = vars, strata = strata, data = d, factorVars = fct_vars,
      addOverall = TRUE, test = TRUE, argsExact = list(workspace = 2 * 10^7))
    small <- fct_vars[vapply(fct_vars, function(v)
      any(table(d[[v]], d[[strata]]) < 5), logical(1))]
    if (!length(small)) small <- NULL
  }

  mat <- print(tab, nonnormal = setdiff(cont_vars, normal_vars), exact = small,
               showAllLevels = TRUE, missing = TRUE, printToggle = FALSE,
               noSpaces = TRUE, quote = FALSE)
  tibble::as_tibble(cbind(Characteristic = rownames(mat), mat),
                    .name_repair = "unique")
}

save_tbl_docx <- function(tbl, docx_name) {
  ft <- gtsummary::as_flex_table(tbl)
  flextable::save_as_docx(ft, path = file.path(docx_dir,
                                               paste0(docx_name, ".docx")))
  invisible(tbl)
}

# Load the Local/Early cohort produced by ritu_data.qmd
dat <- readRDS("ritu_final_master.rds")

# Create eGFR ratio: CKD-EPI Cr-Cys (unindexed) / Cockcroft-Gault
# Also create per-10 mL/min rescaled versions of cockcroft and CKD-EPI for
# reporting (HRs per 1 mL/min are clinically uninterpretable; convention in
# nephro-onc is per 10 mL/min — bio_agent confirmed). Adjusters keep raw scale.
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    # Ratio uses UNCAPPED eGFR
    egfr_ratio    = ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex / cockcroft,
    egfr_ratio_per10 = -egfr_ratio * 10,  # per 0.1-unit *decrease* reporting scale
    egfr_discrepancy = ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex - cockcroft,
    # per-10-mL/min DECLINE reporting scale for eGFR discrepancy: HR for this
    # variable reads as the multiplicative change in subHR per 10 mL/min lower
    # discrepancy (i.e., when CKD-EPI Cr-Cys is 10 mL/min farther below CG).
    egfr_disc_per10dec = -egfr_discrepancy / 10,
    # Sensitivity-analysis eGFR ratio (Section 11):
    # numerator = CKD-EPI 2012 cystatin C only (baseline_cys_c_egfr_unindexed)
    # denominator = CKD-EPI 2021 race-free creatinine only (baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed)
    # (Both unindexed; the ratio itself is invariant to whether indexed or unindexed
    # because BSA cancels.) per10 below is the per-0.1 DECLINE reporting scale.
    egfr_ratio_sens       = baseline_cys_c_egfr_unindexed / baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed,
    egfr_ratio_sens_per10 = -egfr_ratio_sens * 10,
    # Percent-difference eGFR (new primary exposure):
    # egfr_diff_pct = 100 * (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys unindexed - Cockcroft-Gault) / Cockcroft-Gault
    # egfr_diff_pct_per10: HR reads as multiplicative change per 10 percentage-point DECLINE.
    egfr_diff_pct         = 100 * (ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex - cockcroft) / cockcroft,
    egfr_diff_pct_per10   = -egfr_diff_pct / 10,
    # Percent-difference eGFR for sensitivity analysis:
    # numerator - denominator = CKD-EPI 2012 CysC - CKD-EPI 2021 Cr, both unindexed.
    egfr_diff_pct_sens        = 100 * (baseline_cys_c_egfr_unindexed - baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed) / baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed,
    egfr_diff_pct_sens_per10  = -egfr_diff_pct_sens / 10,
    # Binary form of the same exposure: 1 when the cystatin C eGFR sits more
    # than 10 % below the creatinine eGFR. Reference level is ">= -10%".
    egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat    = factor(
      ifelse(egfr_diff_pct_sens < -10, "< -10%", ">= -10%"),
      levels = c(">= -10%", "< -10%")),
    # Stricter cut at -30 %: a much smaller, more clearly discordant group.
    egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat30  = factor(
      ifelse(egfr_diff_pct_sens < -30, "< -30%", ">= -30%"),
      levels = c(">= -30%", "< -30%")),
    # "Survivor": still in follow-up beyond one year.
    survivor_365              = days_last_follow_up > 365,
    cockcroft_per10 = cockcroft / 10,
    ckd_epi_per10   = ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex / 10
  )
```

# 2 Table 1: Baseline Characteristics (Overall + Cisplatin / Carboplatin)

Table 1 is now stratified by `platin_group`. Columns show the overall cohort and the two platinum subgroups side-by-side, with a between-group p-value (Wilcoxon rank-sum for continuous, Fisher exact for categorical with any observed cell < 5, else χ²). The `platin_group`, `carbo_AUC`, and `cis_dose`-related variables are removed from the row list because they are collinear with the stratification column.

**Missing counts.** The final `Missing` column gives each variable's percent missing in the full cohort. In practice this cohort is complete on the entire adjuster / predictor set once record 911 is dropped upstream in `ritu_data.qmd`: `pre_HGB_45days`, `pre_PLT_45days`, `pre_ALB_45days`, and `pre_CRE_45days` all show 0/322 missing, and the age / sex / BMI / smoking / thyroid / steroids / RPDR-comorbidity / eGFR variables are also fully populated. The only NA-by-design variables in the row list are `carbo_AUC` / `carbo_AUC_cat` (NA for cisplatin patients) and `cis_dose` / `cis_dose_high` (NA for carboplatin patients). Consequently, the "Excluded (missing cov.)" column in the Section 4 / 7 / 11 summary tables is 0 for every outcome.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-table1-whole
t1 <- dat %>%
  # Show the numeric KDIGO stage as a labelled factor for Table 1. get_ckd_stage()
  # collapses G3a/G3b into a single stage 3, unlike ckd_stage_cre / ckd_stage_cre_cys.
  mutate(ckd_stage_baseline = droplevels(
           factor(ckd_stage_baseline, levels = 1:5,
                  labels = c("G1 (>=90)", "G2 (60-89)", "G3 (30-59)",
                             "G4 (15-29)", "G5 (<15)")))) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    age, age_cat, sex, race, ethnicity, cancer_type_cat_7,
    platin_group, carbo_AUC, carbo_AUC_cat, cis_dose, cis_dose_high,
    ici, Bevacizumab, Paclitaxel, Pemetrexed, Doxorubicin, Etoposide,
    Gemcitabine, Pertuzumab, Trastuzumab, Docetaxel, other_chemo, Administered_alone,
    hiv_rpdr, thyroid, smoking, steroids, esrd_kt,
    cci, score, ecog_score, bmi, bmi_cat,
    pre_HGB_45days, pre_PLT_45days, pre_ALB_45days, pre_CRE_45days,
    baseline_cys_c, baseline_cre, cr_cys,
    baseline_cre_egfr, baseline_cys_c_egfr,
    ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys, ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex,
    ckd_stage_cre, ckd_stage_cre_cys,
    cockcroft, egfr_ratio,
    # Long-horizon kidney variables (Sections 5.16-5.19 of ritu_data.qmd).
    # eGFR_CRE_baseline / ckd_stage_baseline are baseline; last_cre_days is
    # creatinine follow-up length; the rest are outcomes over that full window,
    # NOT censored at 90 days like every other outcome in this project.
    eGFR_CRE_baseline, ckd_stage_baseline, last_cre_days,
    aki, aki_any, ckd_incidence, ckd_incidence_any, ckd_progression,
    eskd_defination_1, esrd_kt_after_ici, eskd_composite, ckd_composite,
    # Delta eGFR vs baseline at fixed marks (Section 5.16b). Negative =
    # decline. Closest creatinine within +/- 45 days of each mark.
    delta_egfr_d90, delta_egfr_d180, delta_egfr_d365,
    delta_egfr_pct_d90, delta_egfr_pct_d180, delta_egfr_pct_d365
  ) %>%
  tableone_mat(strata = "platin_group")

cap_t1 <- sprintf(paste0(
  "Table 1. Baseline characteristics by platinum group, N = %d. Continuous ",
  "variables are median [IQR] except age, which is mean (SD); categorical ",
  "variables are n (%%). Missing is the percent missing in the full cohort."),
  nrow(dat))

flextable::flextable(t1) |>
  flextable::set_caption(cap_t1) |>
  flextable::fontsize(size = 9, part = "all") |>
  flextable::autofit() |>
  flextable::save_as_docx(path = file.path(docx_dir, "table1.docx"))

knitr::kable(t1, caption = cap_t1)
```

## 2.1 Follow-up time (days from baseline to last known status)

`days_last_follow_up` = `last_follow_up_date − baseline_sample_date`. Two alternative definitions of "follow-up time" are shown side-by-side so the reader can pick the most defensible one for their purpose:

- **A — Raw days**: unrestricted calendar follow-up (median dominated by patients who kept returning for years).
- **B — Raw days, ≤ 365 days**: restricts to patients whose last-known contact was **within 1 year** of baseline (drops the long tail of years-later return visits; more comparable across patients).

```{r}
#| label: ritu-followup-desc-whole
followup_summary <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(record_id, platin_group, days_last_follow_up) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na(days_last_follow_up)

fmt_med_iqr <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0) return("—")
  sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]", median(x), quantile(x, 0.25), quantile(x, 0.75))
}

groups_split <- function(f) {
  x_all <- f(followup_summary$days_last_follow_up)
  x_cis <- f(followup_summary$days_last_follow_up[followup_summary$platin_group == "Cisplatin"])
  x_car <- f(followup_summary$days_last_follow_up[followup_summary$platin_group == "Carboplatin"])
  list(Overall = x_all, Cisplatin = x_cis, Carboplatin = x_car)
}

fu_row <- function(label, xs) {
  tibble::tibble(
    Interpretation                      = label,
    `Overall N`                         = length(xs$Overall),
    `Overall — Median [IQR] (days)`     = fmt_med_iqr(xs$Overall),
    `Cisplatin N`                       = length(xs$Cisplatin),
    `Cisplatin — Median [IQR] (days)`   = fmt_med_iqr(xs$Cisplatin),
    `Carboplatin N`                     = length(xs$Carboplatin),
    `Carboplatin — Median [IQR] (days)` = fmt_med_iqr(xs$Carboplatin)
  )
}

def_A <- function(v) v
def_B <- function(v) v[v <= 365]

followup_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  fu_row("A — Raw days",             groups_split(def_A)),
  fu_row("B — Raw days, ≤ 365 days", groups_split(def_B))
)

flextable::flextable(followup_tbl) |>
  flextable::set_caption("Follow-up time from baseline to last known status (whole cohort). Two alternative definitions shown side-by-side.") |>
  flextable::autofit()
```

## 2.2 Long-Horizon Kidney Outcomes (CKD / ESKD / AKI)

Ported from the [ICI-CKD project](https://tianqi-ouyang.github.io/ICI-CKD-/data_management.html)
and built in Sections 5.16–5.19 of [Data Management](ritu_data.qmd). Creatinine
for these comes from the Ritu_project RPDR pull (Oct 2026).

> **None of these are censored at 90 days.** A qualifying CKD episode has to be
> *sustained for ≥ 90 days*, so they run over the full length of RPDR creatinine
> follow-up. `aki` is restricted to events within 1 year. This section reports all
> of them descriptively; **`aki` and `ckd_composite` are the two that are
> modelled** — see the Fine-Gray section below. The rest are descriptive only.

**Definitions as of the latest revision.** `aki` is now restricted to events
**within 1 year** of baseline (`aki_any` keeps the unrestricted count for
reference and is not modelled). `ckd_incidence` uses a **> 25 %** eGFR drop;
`ckd_incidence_any` drops the percent requirement entirely; `ckd_progression`
now additionally requires a **> 30 %** further drop, where it previously counted
any patient who was simply below 60 before and after — which flagged stable CKD
as progression and is why that count fell sharply.

`aki` is also not the same variable as `AKI_g2_90days` / `AKI_kdigo_90days`: it
compares each creatinine against the patient's own preceding 90-day median (or
2-day low) rather than against a fixed pre-baseline value. The cross-tabulation
below shows how far the two diverge.

[📄 Download Word table](../tables/whole/sec2_kidney_longhorizon.docx)

```{r}
#| label: ritu-kidney-lt
.kid_row <- function(flag, time_var, label) {
  n <- sum(dat[[flag]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  tt <- if (!is.null(time_var) && time_var %in% names(dat))
          dat[[time_var]][dat[[flag]] == 1] else NA_real_
  tibble::tibble(
    Outcome = label,
    `n (%)` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, 100 * n / nrow(dat)),
    `Median days to event (IQR)` = if (n > 0 && any(!is.na(tt)))
        sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", median(tt, na.rm = TRUE),
                quantile(tt, .25, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(tt, .75, na.rm = TRUE))
      else "-"
  )
}

kidney_lt <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  .kid_row("aki",               "aki_days",                    "AKI within 1 year (serial creatinine)"),
  .kid_row("aki_any",           "aki_days_any",                "AKI at any time (reference only, not modelled)"),
  .kid_row("ckd_incidence",     "time_to_ckd_incidence",       "CKD incidence (>25% eGFR drop to <60, sustained >=90d)"),
  .kid_row("ckd_incidence_any", "time_to_ckd_incidence_any",   "CKD incidence any (>=60 to <60, sustained >=90d, no % drop)"),
  .kid_row("ckd_progression",   "time_to_ckd_progression",     "CKD progression (<60 at baseline, further >30% drop, sustained >=90d)"),
  .kid_row("eskd_defination_1", NULL,                          "ESKD (eGFR <10, sustained >=90d)"),
  .kid_row("esrd_kt_after_ici", NULL,                          "ESRD / kidney transplant after baseline"),
  .kid_row("eskd_composite",    "time_to_eskd_composite",      "ESKD composite"),
  .kid_row("ckd_composite",     "time_to_ckd_composite",       "CKD composite (incidence + progression + ESKD composite)")
)

ft_kid <- flextable::flextable(kidney_lt) |>
  flextable::set_caption(sprintf(
    "Long-horizon kidney outcomes (N = %d). Not censored at 90 days.", nrow(dat))) |>
  flextable::autofit()
flextable::save_as_docx(ft_kid, path = file.path(docx_dir, "sec2_kidney_longhorizon.docx"))
ft_kid
```

Creatinine follow-up actually available for these outcomes, and how the two AKI
definitions compare:

```{r}
#| label: ritu-kidney-lt-fu
cat(sprintf("Days from baseline to last creatinine: median %.0f (IQR %.0f-%.0f), max %.0f\n",
            median(dat$last_cre_days, na.rm = TRUE),
            quantile(dat$last_cre_days, .25, na.rm = TRUE),
            quantile(dat$last_cre_days, .75, na.rm = TRUE),
            max(dat$last_cre_days, na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("Patients with no post-baseline creatinine: %d\n",
            sum(is.na(dat$last_cre_days))))
cat("\nSerial-creatinine AKI (rows) vs 90-day KDIGO AKI (columns):\n")
print(table(`serial aki` = dat$aki, `AKI_kdigo_90days` = dat$AKI_kdigo_90days))
```

## 2.3 Delta eGFR (creatinine) vs Baseline at 90 / 180 / 365 Days

Change in creatinine eGFR from `eGFR_CRE_baseline`, using the creatinine
**closest to each mark** and taking it only when it falls within **± 45 days**
of that mark. Days run from `baseline_sample_date`. Built in Section 5.16b of
[Data Management](ritu_data.qmd).

> **Negative means decline.** `delta_egfr_d90` is eGFR at day 90 minus eGFR at
> baseline, so a fall in kidney function is a negative number — the opposite sign
> to `pct_drop` in the data-management pipeline.
>
> The ± 45-day window matches the window used for every other baseline lab in
> this pipeline (`pre_CRE_45days`), and it is the widest window that stops the
> 90-day and 180-day marks drawing on the same measurement. It costs coverage at
> the later marks — the `n` column below shows how much.

[📄 Download Word table](../tables/whole/sec2_3_delta_egfr.docx)

```{r}
#| label: ritu-delta-egfr
dgfr_marks <- c(90, 180, 365)

dgfr_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(dgfr_marks, function(mk) {
  d  <- dat[[paste0("delta_egfr_d", mk)]]
  dp <- dat[[paste0("delta_egfr_pct_d", mk)]]
  dy <- dat[[paste0("cre_day_d", mk)]]
  g  <- dat[[paste0("eGFR_CRE_d", mk)]]
  ok <- !is.na(d)
  q3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]",
         median(x), quantile(x, .25), quantile(x, .75))
  tibble::tibble(
    Mark = paste0("Day ", mk),
    n = sum(ok),
    `% with a value in window` = round(100 * sum(ok) / nrow(dat), 1),
    `Actual day` = sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]",
      median(dy[ok]), quantile(dy[ok], .25), quantile(dy[ok], .75)),
    `eGFR at mark` = q3(g[ok]),
    `Delta eGFR` = q3(d[ok]),
    `Delta eGFR (%)` = q3(dp[ok])
  )
})

ft_dgfr <- flextable::flextable(dgfr_tbl) |>
  flextable::set_caption(sprintf(paste0(
    "Delta eGFR (creatinine) vs baseline, N = %d. eGFR in mL/min/1.73m², ",
    "median [IQR] throughout. Negative = decline from baseline."), nrow(dat))) |>
  flextable::autofit()
flextable::save_as_docx(ft_dgfr, path = file.path(docx_dir, "sec2_3_delta_egfr.docx"))
ft_dgfr
```

**Who is missing, and why.** The marks are only as good as the creatinine
follow-up behind them. The first table below shows which of the three marks each
patient covers; the second shows how many creatinines those patients had and how
far their follow-up reached.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-delta-egfr-coverage
.pat <- paste0(dat$dgfr_avail_d90, dat$dgfr_avail_d180, dat$dgfr_avail_d365)
.k   <- dat$dgfr_avail_d90 + dat$dgfr_avail_d180 + dat$dgfr_avail_d365

pat_lv <- c("111", "110", "101", "011", "100", "010", "001", "000")
pat_lb <- c("All three", "Day 90 + 180", "Day 90 + 365", "Day 180 + 365",
            "Day 90 only", "Day 180 only", "Day 365 only", "None of the three")

cov_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  `Marks with a value` = pat_lb,
  n = as.integer(table(factor(.pat, levels = pat_lv)))
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(`% of cohort` = round(100 * n / nrow(dat), 1))

knitr::kable(cov_tbl, caption = sprintf(paste0(
  "Which of the three marks each patient has a creatinine for, N = %d. ",
  "A mark counts only when a creatinine falls within ± 45 days of it."), nrow(dat)))
```

```{r}
#| label: ritu-delta-egfr-coverage-why
.iqr <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (!length(x)) return("—")
  sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]", median(x), quantile(x, .25), quantile(x, .75))
}

why_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(0:3, function(k) {
  i <- .k == k
  tibble::tibble(
    `Marks covered` = paste0(k, " of 3"),
    n = sum(i),
    `% of cohort` = round(100 * sum(i) / nrow(dat), 1),
    `No post-baseline creatinine at all` = sum(i & dat$n_cre_post == 0),
    `Post-baseline creatinines, median [IQR]` = .iqr(dat$n_cre_post[i]),
    `Last creatinine, day, median [IQR]` = .iqr(dat$last_cre_days[i])
  )
})

knitr::kable(why_tbl, caption = sprintf(paste0(
  "Why marks are missed, N = %d. Patients are grouped by how many of the three ",
  "marks they cover. The last column is the day of their final creatinine."), nrow(dat)))
```


# 3 eGFR Ratio and Discordance Distributions (Overall)

## 3.1 eGFR Ratio distribution

Red bins highlight the region **below ratio = 1** (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys eGFR below Cockcroft-Gault, consistent with muscle-wasting / sarcopenia); gray bins are the region above.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-egfr-ratio-lt09-count
#| results: asis
n_lt <- sum(dat$egfr_ratio < 0.9, na.rm = TRUE)
n_av <- sum(!is.na(dat$egfr_ratio))
cat(sprintf(
  "> **eGFR ratio < 0.9:** %d / %d (%.1f%%) of the whole cohort.\n",
  n_lt, n_av, 100 * n_lt / n_av))
```

```{r}
#| label: ritu-egfr-ratio-hist
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
ratio_hist <- dat %>%
  filter(!is.na(egfr_ratio)) %>%
  mutate(side = ifelse(egfr_ratio < 1, "neg", "pos"))

ggplot(ratio_hist, aes(x = egfr_ratio, fill = side)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(count) / sum(after_stat(count)) * 100),
                 binwidth = 0.1, boundary = 0,
                 color = "black", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(neg = "#E31A1C", pos = "grey60"),
                    guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of eGFR Ratio (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys unindexed / Cockcroft-Gault)",
       x = "eGFR Ratio",
       y = "Percent of Patients (%)") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 3, 0.2)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

## 3.2 eGFR Discordance distribution

Signed eGFR discordance = CKD-EPI Cr-Cys unindexed − Cockcroft-Gault (mL/min). Red bins highlight the negative side (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys **below** Cockcroft-Gault — the direction that flags reduced cystatin-based eGFR relative to creatinine-based, consistent with muscle wasting / sarcopenia); gray bins are the positive side.

```{r}

       x = "eGFR Discordance (mL/min)",

```

Signed eGFR difference (%) = 100 × (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys unindexed − Cockcroft-Gault) / Cockcroft-Gault. Concordance sits at 0 %. Red bins highlight the negative side (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys below CG by more than 0 %, consistent with muscle wasting / sarcopenia); gray bins are the positive side.

## 3.4 eGFR Difference (sens) distribution

Signed eGFR difference (sens) = 100 × (CKD-EPI 2012 cystatin C − CKD-EPI 2021
creatinine) / CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine, both unindexed. Concordance sits at 0 %.
Red bins are the negative side — cystatin C below creatinine, the
muscle-wasting direction. The dashed line at **− 10 %** is the cut used for the
binary exposure further down.

```{r}

  scale_fill_manual(values = c(neg = "#E31A1C", pos = "grey60"), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of eGFR Difference (sens): 100 × (CysC − Cr) / Cr",
       subtitle = sprintf("Median %.1f %%; %d of %d (%.1f %%) fall below -10 %%",
                          median(diffsens_hist$egfr_diff_pct_sens),
                          sum(diffsens_hist$egfr_diff_pct_sens < -10),
                          nrow(diffsens_hist),
                          100 * mean(diffsens_hist$egfr_diff_pct_sens < -10)),
       x = "eGFR Difference (sens, %)", y = "Percent of Patients (%)") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-100, 200, 10)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

# 4 Fine-Gray Models — eGFR Difference as (CysC − Cr) / Cr, adjusted for CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine eGFR (unindexed, mL/min)

> **These are the only two outcomes modelled on this page.** Both run on the
> long-horizon kidney outcomes built in Sections 5.16–5.19 of
> [Data Management](ritu_data.qmd):
> AKI is administratively censored at **365 days**, the CKD composite runs to the
> **last creatinine** (day 0 → last follow-up). Death at any time is the
> competing event in both, taken from `death_days_any` rather than the 90-day
> `death_90` flag, which cannot place a death in time beyond day 90.
> `death_days_any` is the union of the two sources that carry a death date — the
> RPDR `Date_Of_Death` when there is one, otherwise the REDCap last-follow-up
> date for a patient REDCap records as dead. Someone flagged deceased in RPDR
> with no date who is still alive in REDCap stays censored.
>
> **The exposure in both sections below is `egfr_diff_pct_sens_per10`** —
> `100 × (eGFR_CysC − eGFR_Cr) / eGFR_Cr`, negated and divided by 10, so every
> subdistribution hazard ratio reads per **10 percentage-point decline**.
> Cystatin C against creatinine alone, both unindexed. The two sections differ
> only in the kidney adjuster: creatinine eGFR in absolute mL/min here,
> indexed to body surface area in the next.
> All other adjusters are the project's standard set (Section 1).

Each table shows univariable (one variable at a time) and multivariable Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard ratios side-by-side. A Word version of each table is saved during render — the download link sits under its heading.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-fg-helper
.adj_set <- function(pred_var, pre_labs, egfr_adj) {
  adj <- c("age","sex","score","ecog_score_cat2",
           "cancer_type_cat_7","platin_group","high_dose",
           "Paclitaxel","Pemetrexed","Gemcitabine","ici",
           "bmi","smoking","thyroid")
  # Drop platin_group when predictor requires dose data (carbo-only after drop_na)
  if (grepl("dose_discrep", pred_var)) adj <- setdiff(adj, "platin_group")
  if (egfr_adj == "cockcroft") adj <- c(adj, "cockcroft")
  if (egfr_adj == "ckd_epi")   adj <- c(adj, "ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex")
  # Indexed to BSA (mL/min/1.73m2), as opposed to the absolute mL/min above.
  if (egfr_adj == "ckd_epi_idx") adj <- c(adj, "ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys")
  # Creatinine-only CKD-EPI 2021, race-free. Unlike the Cr-Cys forms above
  # it shares no measurement with the exposure.
  if (egfr_adj == "cre")     adj <- c(adj, "baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed")
  if (egfr_adj == "cre_idx") adj <- c(adj, "baseline_cre_egfr")
  if (!is.null(pre_labs)) adj <- c(adj, pre_labs)
  adj
}

# fg_model: returns univariable + multivariable merged Fine-Gray table.
# If docx_name is supplied, also saves the table as a .docx in docx_dir.
fg_model <- function(time_var, status_var, pred_var, pre_labs = NULL,
                     egfr_adj = c("none", "cockcroft", "ckd_epi", "ckd_epi_idx",
                                  "cre", "cre_idx"),
                     docx_name = NULL) {
  egfr_adj <- match.arg(egfr_adj)
  adj <- .adj_set(pred_var, pre_labs, egfr_adj)
  all_vars <- c(pred_var, adj)

  # Multivariable
  fmla_mv <- as.formula(paste0(
    "Surv(", time_var, ", ", status_var, ") ~ ",
    paste(all_vars, collapse = " + ")
  ))
  tbl_mv <- tidycmprsk::crr(fmla_mv, failcode = 1, data = dat) %>%
    tbl_regression(exp = TRUE,
                   pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)) %>%
    add_n()

  # Univariable: one Fine-Gray fit per variable
  y_call <- str2lang(sprintf("Surv(%s, %s)", time_var, status_var))
  tbl_uv <- rlang::inject(
    tbl_uvregression(
      data = dat,
      method = tidycmprsk::crr,
      y = !!y_call,
      include = dplyr::all_of(all_vars),
      exponentiate = TRUE,
      pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3),
      method.args = list(failcode = 1)
    )
  )

  out <- tbl_merge(
    tbls = list(tbl_uv, tbl_mv),
    tab_spanner = c("**Univariable**", "**Multivariable**")
  )

  if (!is.null(docx_name)) save_tbl_docx(out, docx_name)
  out
}
# Ritu: guard against unfittable sparse-outcome models.
fg_model <- .wrap_tbl(fg_model)


# cox_model: same signature/output for the 90-day death analysis (Cox PH).
cox_model <- function(time_var, status_var, pred_var, pre_labs = NULL,
                      egfr_adj = c("none", "cockcroft", "ckd_epi", "ckd_epi_idx",
                                  "cre", "cre_idx"),
                      docx_name = NULL) {
  egfr_adj <- match.arg(egfr_adj)
  adj <- .adj_set(pred_var, pre_labs, egfr_adj)
  all_vars <- c(pred_var, adj)

  fmla_mv <- as.formula(paste0(
    "Surv(", time_var, ", ", status_var, ") ~ ",
    paste(all_vars, collapse = " + ")
  ))
  tbl_mv <- survival::coxph(fmla_mv, data = dat) %>%
    tbl_regression(exp = TRUE,
                   pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)) %>%
    add_n()

  y_call <- str2lang(sprintf("Surv(%s, %s)", time_var, status_var))
  tbl_uv <- rlang::inject(
    tbl_uvregression(
      data = dat,
      method = survival::coxph,
      y = !!y_call,
      include = dplyr::all_of(all_vars),
      exponentiate = TRUE,
      pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)
    )
  )

  out <- tbl_merge(
    tbls = list(tbl_uv, tbl_mv),
    tab_spanner = c("**Univariable**", "**Multivariable**")
  )

  if (!is.null(docx_name)) save_tbl_docx(out, docx_name)
  out
}
# Ritu: guard against unfittable sparse-outcome models.
cox_model <- .wrap_tbl(cox_model)

```

# 5 Fine-Gray Models — eGFR Difference as (CysC − Cr) / Cr, adjusted for CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine eGFR (indexed, mL/min/1.73m²)

> Identical to the section above in every respect but one: the kidney adjuster
> is **`baseline_cre_egfr`** — CKD-EPI 2021 race-free creatinine **indexed
> to body surface area, mL/min/1.73m²** — where the section above uses
> `baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed`, the same estimate in absolute mL/min.
>
> Same exposure (`egfr_diff_pct_sens_per10`, per 10 percentage-point decline),
> same two outcomes, same competing event, same remaining covariates. The two
> sections therefore isolate what the BSA indexing of the adjuster does. The two
> forms correlate at 0.83, so they are related but not interchangeable.
>
> Cockcroft-Gault is no longer an adjuster in either section.

# 6 Survivors Cohort — Follow-up > 365 Days

> The Fine-Gray models above, rerun on patients still in follow-up beyond one
> year (`days_last_follow_up > 365`). Adjusted for **`baseline_cre_egfr`**
> (indexed, mL/min/1.73m²); same exposure and competing event, only the cohort
> changes.
>
> **This conditions on a post-baseline characteristic.** Surviving and staying in
> follow-up past a year is partly a consequence of the kidney trajectory being
> modelled, so this subset is not a random sample and these estimates are not
> directly comparable with the full-cohort ones above. Read it as a restriction
> analysis, not a sensitivity analysis.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-surv-enter

dat <- dat_full_cohort %>%
  filter(!is.na(days_last_follow_up), days_last_follow_up > 365) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.factor) & !starts_with("cmp_status_"), droplevels))

  Outcome  = c("AKI within 1 year", "CKD composite (any time)"),
  Censored = c(sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365 == 0), sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite == 0)),
  Event    = c(sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365 == 1), sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite == 1)),
  Death    = c(sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365 == 2), sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite == 2))
)
knitr::kable(surv_counts, caption = sprintf(
  "Survivors cohort: %d of %d patients (%.1f %%). Competing-risk event counts.",
  nrow(dat), nrow(dat_full_cohort), 100 * nrow(dat) / nrow(dat_full_cohort)))
```

# 7 Binary eGFR Difference (sens) — AKI and CKD Composite

> The same two outcomes and the same adjusters as the Fine-Gray sections above,
> with the exposure entered as a **binary split** rather than per 10
> percentage-point decline.
>
> - `egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat` splits at **− 10 %** — `< -10%` means the cystatin C
>   eGFR sits more than 10 % below the creatinine eGFR; `>= -10%` is the
>   reference.
> - `egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat30` splits at **− 30 %**, a smaller and more clearly
>   discordant group.
>
> Each subdistribution hazard ratio is therefore for the exposed group **against
> its reference group**, not per unit. Death at any time is the competing event
> and the kidney adjuster is `baseline_cre_egfr` (indexed, mL/min/1.73m²), as
> in the sections above.

## 7.1 Prevalence of the two cuts

```{r}
#| label: ritu-bin-prev
.cut_row <- function(v, lab) tibble::tibble(
  Cut = lab, Exposed = sum(v), Unexposed = sum(!v),
  `% exposed` = round(100 * mean(v), 1),
  `AKI events, exposed`   = sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365[v]  == 1),
  `AKI events, unexposed` = sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365[!v] == 1),
  `CKD events, exposed`   = sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite[v]  == 1),
  `CKD events, unexposed` = sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite[!v] == 1))

cut_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  .cut_row(dat$egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat   == "< -10%", "< -10% (primary)"),
  .cut_row(dat$egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat30 == "< -30%", "< -30% (stricter)"))

knitr::kable(cut_tbl, caption = sprintf(
  "Prevalence of the two binary cuts, N = %d. Median eGFR difference (sens) %.1f %%.",
  nrow(dat), median(dat$egfr_diff_pct_sens, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

The four models above, repeated on the **survivors cohort**
(`days_last_follow_up > 365`). Same exposures, outcomes, adjusters and competing
event; only the cohort changes. As in the survivors section earlier, this
conditions on a post-baseline characteristic, so these are a restriction
analysis rather than a sensitivity check.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-binsurv-enter
dat_full_cohort <- dat
dat <- dat_full_cohort %>%
  filter(!is.na(days_last_follow_up), days_last_follow_up > 365) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.factor) & !starts_with("cmp_status_"), droplevels))

binsurv <- purrr::map_dfr(
  list(c("< -10%", "egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat"), c("< -30%", "egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat30")),
  function(z) {
    e <- dat[[z[2]]] == z[1]
    tibble::tibble(Cut = z[1], `n survivors` = nrow(dat),
                   Exposed = sum(e), Unexposed = sum(!e),
                   `AKI events, exposed`   = sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365[e]  == 1),
                   `AKI events, unexposed` = sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365[!e] == 1),
                   `CKD events, exposed`   = sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite[e]  == 1),
                   `CKD events, unexposed` = sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite[!e] == 1))
  })
knitr::kable(binsurv, caption = sprintf(
  "Survivors cohort: %d of %d patients. Exposed-group event counts behind the four models below.",
  nrow(dat), nrow(dat_full_cohort)))
```

# 9 CG vs CKD-EPI Cr-Cys (highlighted by Age / BMI)

For each plot below, the x-axis is Cockcroft-Gault eGFR (mL/min) and the y-axis is CKD-EPI Cr-Cys *unindexed* eGFR (mL/min). The dashed line is `y = x` (perfect agreement). Patients meeting the highlighted threshold are coloured red; all others are grey. `N` shown in each title is the count of patients with both eGFR values non-missing; `n_red` is the count meeting the red criterion.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-scatter-cg-epi-helper
plot_cg_vs_epi <- function(highlight_var, threshold, label) {
  d <- dat %>%
    filter(!is.na(cockcroft), !is.na(ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex),
           !is.na(.data[[highlight_var]])) %>%
    mutate(highlight = .data[[highlight_var]] >= threshold)

  n_total <- nrow(d)
  n_red   <- sum(d$highlight)

  # Fit two separate OLS models so we can annotate each with its equation + R².
  fit_true  <- lm(ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex ~ cockcroft,
                  data = d %>% filter(highlight))
  fit_false <- lm(ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex ~ cockcroft,
                  data = d %>% filter(!highlight))
  eq_str <- function(fit) {
    b  <- coef(fit)
    r2 <- summary(fit)$r.squared
    sprintf("y = %.2f x %+.1f   (R² = %.2f)", b[2], b[1], r2)
  }

  ggplot(d, aes(x = cockcroft, y = ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex,
                color = highlight, fill = highlight)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.6) +
    # One OLS regression line per level of `highlight` (colour + CI ribbon
    # match the dot colour).
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE,
                alpha = 0.15, linewidth = 1) +
    annotate("text", x = 5, y = 195, hjust = 0, size = 3.4,
             color = "#E31A1C", label = paste0(">= threshold: ", eq_str(fit_true))) +
    annotate("text", x = 5, y = 182, hjust = 0, size = 3.4,
             color = "grey40",  label = paste0("< threshold:  ", eq_str(fit_false))) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey60", "TRUE" = "#E31A1C"),
                       guide = "none") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey60", "TRUE" = "#E31A1C"),
                      guide = "none") +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 200), ylim = c(0, 200)) +
    labs(x = "Cockcroft-Gault eGFR (mL/min)",
         y = "CKD-EPI Cr-Cys eGFR, unindexed (mL/min)",
         title = sprintf("%s   |   N = %d, n_red = %d",
                         label, n_total, n_red)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
}
```

## 9.7 – 9.12 eGFR Difference (%) distribution by category

For each of the same six splits as 10.1 – 10.6, overlaid kernel density curves of the eGFR difference (%) = 100 × (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys unindexed − Cockcroft-Gault) / Cockcroft-Gault. Red = highlighted level (≥ threshold, or Female for the sex panel); grey = reference level. Dashed grey vertical line marks the 0 % concordance point; dotted verticals mark each group's median. Subtitle carries N and median for each level plus a two-sided Mann-Whitney U p-value (equivalent to Wilcoxon rank-sum) comparing the two distributions.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-ratio-by-group-helper
plot_ratio_by_group <- function(highlight_var, threshold, label,
                                highlight_label, reference_label) {
  d <- dat %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(egfr_diff_pct), !is.na(.data[[highlight_var]])) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(grp = factor(
      ifelse(.data[[highlight_var]] >= threshold, highlight_label, reference_label),
      levels = c(highlight_label, reference_label)))

  med_tbl <- d %>%
    dplyr::group_by(grp) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(m = median(egfr_diff_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
                     n = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop")

  pval <- tryCatch(
    wilcox.test(egfr_diff_pct ~ grp, data = d)$p.value,
    error = function(e) NA_real_)
  p_str <- if (is.na(pval)) "NA" else
    ifelse(pval < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", pval))

  col_vec <- setNames(c("#E31A1C", "grey50"),
                      c(highlight_label, reference_label))

  ggplot(d, aes(x = egfr_diff_pct, fill = grp, color = grp)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
    geom_vline(data = med_tbl, aes(xintercept = m, color = grp),
               linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = col_vec) +
    scale_color_manual(values = col_vec) +
    labs(x = "eGFR difference (%): 100 × (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys − CG) / CG",
         y = "Density",
         fill = NULL, color = NULL,
         title = label,
         subtitle = sprintf(
           "%s: N = %d, median = %.1f %%   |   %s: N = %d, median = %.1f %%   |   Mann-Whitney U p = %s",
           highlight_label,
           med_tbl$n[med_tbl$grp == highlight_label],
           med_tbl$m[med_tbl$grp == highlight_label],
           reference_label,
           med_tbl$n[med_tbl$grp == reference_label],
           med_tbl$m[med_tbl$grp == reference_label],
           p_str)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "top",
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey25"))
}
```

# 10 365-Day Delta eGFR on the Binary eGFR Difference (sens)

> The outcome is `delta_egfr_d365` — eGFR at day 365 minus baseline, in
> mL/min/1.73m², **negative = decline** (see the Delta eGFR table above). Only
> patients with a creatinine within ± 45 days of day 365 contribute, so every
> model in this section is complete-case on that variable and its n is well
> below the cohort.
>
> Both cuts of `egfr_diff_pct_sens` are reported: the primary one at **− 10 %**
> and the stricter one at **− 30 %**. `< -10%` means the cystatin C eGFR sits
> more than 10 % below the creatinine eGFR; `>= -10%` is the reference level.

## 10.1 365-day delta eGFR by group — cut at − 10 %

```{r}
#| label: ritu-cat-groups
.grp_row <- function(d, lab) {
  v <- d$delta_egfr_d365[!is.na(d$delta_egfr_d365)]
  p <- d$delta_egfr_pct_d365[!is.na(d$delta_egfr_pct_d365)]
  tibble::tibble(
    Group = lab, n = length(v),
    `Delta eGFR, mean (SD)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(v), sd(v)),
    `Delta eGFR, median [IQR]` = sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]",
      median(v), quantile(v, .25), quantile(v, .75)),
    `Delta eGFR %, median [IQR]` = sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]",
      median(p), quantile(p, .25), quantile(p, .75)))
}
d0 <- dat %>% filter(egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat == ">= -10%")
d1 <- dat %>% filter(egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat == "< -10%")
grp_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(.grp_row(d0, ">= -10% (reference)"), .grp_row(d1, "< -10%"))

.wt <- tryCatch(wilcox.test(delta_egfr_d365 ~ egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat, data = dat),
                error = function(e) NULL)
.tt <- tryCatch(t.test(delta_egfr_d365 ~ egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat, data = dat),
                error = function(e) NULL)
knitr::kable(grp_tbl, caption = sprintf(paste0(
  "365-day delta eGFR by binary eGFR difference (sens). Negative = decline. ",
  "Wilcoxon p = %s; Welch t-test p = %s."),
  if (is.null(.wt)) "—" else format.pval(.wt$p.value, digits = 3),
  if (is.null(.tt)) "—" else format.pval(.tt$p.value, digits = 3)))
```

## 10.2 Linear model — cut at − 10 %

Adjusted for the same multivariable covariate set as the Fine-Gray models,
including the same kidney adjuster — `baseline_cre_egfr`, CKD-EPI 2021
race-free creatinine indexed to body surface area (mL/min/1.73m²). Coefficients are mL/min/1.73m² of
365-day eGFR change: a negative coefficient on `< -10%` means that group
declined further.

[📄 Download Word table](../tables/whole/sec10_lm_d365.docx)

```{r}
#| label: ritu-cat-lm
# .adj_set has three arguments on the whole/entire pages and two on the
# carboplatin pages; call it with whichever this page defines.
.adj_for <- function(pred_var, egfr_adj) {
  if (length(formals(.adj_set)) == 3) .adj_set(pred_var, NULL, egfr_adj)
  else .adj_set(NULL, egfr_adj)
}

lm_d365 <- function(pred_var, egfr_adj = "cre_idx", docx_name = NULL) {
  adj  <- .adj_for(pred_var, egfr_adj)
  vars <- c(pred_var, adj)
  fmla <- as.formula(paste("delta_egfr_d365 ~", paste(vars, collapse = " + ")))
  tbl_mv <- lm(fmla, data = dat) %>%
    tbl_regression(pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)) %>%
    add_n()
  tbl_uv <- tbl_uvregression(
    data = dat %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c("delta_egfr_d365", vars))),
    method = lm, y = delta_egfr_d365,
    pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3))
  out <- tbl_merge(tbls = list(tbl_uv, tbl_mv),
                   tab_spanner = c("**Univariable**", "**Multivariable**"))
  if (!is.null(docx_name)) save_tbl_docx(out, docx_name)
  out
}
lm_d365 <- .wrap_tbl(lm_d365)

lm_d365("egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat", docx_name = "sec10_lm_d365")
```

## 10.3 Linear model — cut at − 10 %, survivors cohort

```{r}
dat <- dat_full_cohort %>%
  filter(!is.na(days_last_follow_up), days_last_follow_up > 365) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.factor) & !starts_with("cmp_status_"), droplevels))
out <- lm_d365("egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat", docx_name = "sec10_lm_d365_surv")
dat <- dat_full_cohort
out
```

```{r}
                  error = function(e) NULL)

                  error = function(e) NULL)
knitr::kable(grp30, caption = sprintf(paste0(
  "365-day delta eGFR by the stricter -30 %% cut. Negative = decline. ",
  "Wilcoxon p = %s; Welch t-test p = %s."),
```

## 10.5 Linear model — cut at − 30 %

[📄 Download Word table](../tables/whole/sec10_lm_d365_c30.docx)
